findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting row exists
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` calls `[]` on nil whenever the query returns no rows. That happens on any site where `embed_category` was never changed from its default, because no `site_settings` row exists. The migration then fails with NoMethodError, so the table creation and the whole deploy fail. The fallback query on line 15 has the same problem if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Fix: take `.first` of the result, handle nil, and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` or the category with id 1.

findings.title: Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT SQL
findings.body: Each line of the old setting is put straight into the SQL string. A value with a single quote breaks the migration, and a crafted value can run injected SQL. The lines are also not stripped or normalized, so entries like `http://discourse.org` or `host/path`, or ones with trailing whitespace, are stored raw and never match. The raw insert skips the model's `before_validation` normalization. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h.strip)` or a parameterized insert, and normalize the host (strip scheme and path) first.

findings.title: Missing record gives a 500 instead of a 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `.where(id: ...).first` and then use the result without a nil check. A stale or unknown id, such as a host already deleted in another admin tab, raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` so it returns a 404. In `save_host`, `params[:embeddable_host]` is also dereferenced without a presence check.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil. The admin controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is nil if the param is omitted. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` also raises instead of returning a validation error. Guard with `return if host.nil?` or use non-mutating assignment, for example `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input and ignores ports
findings.body: The column is wrapped in `lower(host)`, but the URI host is not downcased. A referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/` will not match a stored `eviltrout.com`. The validation allows `host:port`, but `URI#host` drops the port, so such entries can never match. Downcase the input, and either reject ports or compare against host plus port.
